questions.question: You want the report title centred over A1:E1 but every cell to stay separate for sorting and pasting. What do you use?

answerOptions.rationale: This merges the cells, which gets in the way of selecting, sorting and pasting.
Wrap Text breaks long text into lines inside one cell; it does not centre across cells.
Format Painter copies an existing look; it does not centre the title.

answerOptions.text: Format Cells (⌘ + 1) > Alignment > Horizontal: Center Across Selection
answerOptions.rationale: It gives the same centred look without merging the cells.

questions.question: Which custom number format shows 2 April 2026 as 02-Apr-26?

answerOptions.rationale: Two m's give the month as a number: 02-04-26.
Three m's give the short month name and two y's give a two-digit year.
Four m's give the full month name and four y's the full year: 02-April-2026.
This puts the month first: 04-02-26.

questions.question: A GST rate cell formatted as Percentage shows 1800%. What went wrong?

answerOptions.rationale: A narrow column shows #### or cuts digits; it does not multiply the value.

answerOptions.text: The format has too many decimal places
answerOptions.rationale: Decimal places change precision, not the size of the number.

answerOptions.text: Someone typed 18 instead of 18%, so the cell holds 18 rather than 0.18
answerOptions.rationale: Percentage format shows the stored value times 100, and 18 times 100 is 1800.

answerOptions.text: Excel cannot show GST rates as percentages
answerOptions.rationale: Percentage format works well for rates once 18% is entered correctly.

questions.question: Which number format lines up every ₹ sign on the left of the cell and shows zero as a dash?

answerOptions.rationale: Accounting aligns symbols and decimals and shows zero as a dash, which suits financial statements.
Currency puts the ₹ sign right next to the number and shows zero as ₹0.00.
Number format has no currency symbol.
General shows the value as typed, with no symbol or alignment rules.

questions.question: Marketing spend of 845000 is formatted with "₹"#,##0.0,"K". What does the cell show?

answerOptions.rationale: The comma after the digits divides by 1,000, and K is a text label.
That would need division by 1,00,000, which a single comma does not do.
The trailing comma divides by a thousand, so the full number is not shown.
That would mean dividing by a million, which needs two trailing commas.

questions.question: After switching the theme, the title and table changed colour but A2 kept its dark blue. Why?

answerOptions.text: Themes only change fonts, never colours
answerOptions.rationale: A theme sets both colours and fonts for the workbook.
Merging does not stop a cell from following the theme.

answerOptions.text: A2 was coloured by hand with a fixed colour, which does not follow the theme
answerOptions.rationale: Cell styles and table styles use theme colours; hand-picked standard colours stay fixed.

answerOptions.text: Themes apply only to the first row
answerOptions.rationale: A theme affects every cell that uses theme colours, wherever it is.

questions.question: You want row 1 and column A to stay visible while you scroll. Which cell do you select before View > Freeze Panes?

answerOptions.rationale: This freezes only row 1, not column A.
Excel freezes everything above and to the left of the selected cell: row 1 and column A.
This freezes only column A, not row 1.
This freezes nine rows, which eats half the screen.

questions.question: You are adding product photos to a catalogue table that will be sorted and filtered. How should you insert them?

answerOptions.rationale: A floating picture stays put while the data moves when you sort.

answerOptions.text: Insert > Shapes, then fill the shape with the photo
answerOptions.rationale: A shape also floats over the grid and does not move with its row.

answerOptions.text: Paste the photo into a comment
answerOptions.rationale: Comments are not shown in the table and do not suit a catalogue.
The photo becomes the cell's content, so it moves with its row.
